description: A group of reads and writes that commits as a whole or not at all (`BEGIN` ... `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`).
Collects the changes of a business operation and writes them in one commit.
Two operations read the same value, both write a result based on it, and one write silently overwrites the other.
How much concurrent transactions can see of each other: Read Committed (Postgres default), Repeatable Read, Serializable.
Locks the selected rows until the transaction ends, so concurrent writers wait instead of overwriting.
A `version` column checked in `UPDATE ... WHERE version = $n`; zero affected rows means someone else changed the row first.
Write the event to an `outbox` table in the same transaction, and publish it afterwards, so data and messages never disagree.
